newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - June 27.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on June 27. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto has asked Indonesians to fight against illegal drugs.
State Secretary Murdiono has denied that foreign mining contractors would have to give the government a 10 percent share of their ventures on a free carried-interest basis.

President Suharto has told Syrian Prime Minister Mahmoud Al-Zoubi that Indonesia will not establish diplomatic ties with Israel as long as there is no comprehensive and just solution between Arab countries and Israel.
A leader of the separatist movement in East Timor, David Alex, has been captured by the military and died of his wounds.

Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo foresees a drop in state-approved foreign investment for the 1997 calendar year from the 1996 figure of $29.9 billion. Earlier this month, the government approved foreign investment proposals ammounting to $14.4 billion in the first five months of the year, a drop of 25.5 percent over the same period last year.
